technical_and_design_decisions: For the U1 landing page, reuse the existing Spring XD AngularJS UI framework and pre-built navigation components to minimize custom code and ensure consistency with the existing UI design system.

For U2 retry configuration, leverage Spring Retry's built-in exception-based retry policy extension point to add configurable retryable exception lists, and add explicit logic to skip retries for Kryo deserialization failures.

For library updates (U3, U4, U5), use Maven dependency management to bump version numbers, and rely on the existing Spring XD integration test suite to validate compatibility, with no planned changes to public module APIs for these minor/patch version updates.

For U6 module/container id exposure, inject the ids as standard Spring environment properties and OS environment variables, following the existing pattern used for other module-level metadata like the module name.

For U7 Kafka bus property overrides, map new user-facing properties directly to native Spring Kafka consumer and producer configuration options, with deployment-time validation to reject invalid values early.

For U8 RPM script consolidation, structure the single repository with separate top-level directories for base XD RPMs and XD+Ambari RPMs to maintain clear separation of concerns, and update existing CI/CD pipelines to point to the new repository location.
assumptions: The third-party library updates (Spring Integration 4.1.5, Spring Integration Kafka 1.2.0, Spring Hadoop 2.2.0 GA) have no breaking API changes that require modifications to existing Spring XD module code.
The existing Spring XD UI codebase is built with AngularJS 1.x, which supports adding new views and navigation links without requiring a full UI framework upgrade.

The existing Spring XD Kafka bus implementation is built on Spring Kafka, so the new consumer/producer properties can be mapped directly to native Spring Kafka configuration options without custom implementation work.
The existing RPM build scripts are compatible with being migrated to a single Git repository without requiring changes to the underlying rpmbuild or Maven build tooling configuration.

The Spring XD module runtime already injects standard module metadata (e.g., module name) into the module application context, so adding module id and container id follows the same established injection pattern.

The RabbitMessageBus retry logic is implemented using Spring Retry, so adding configurable retryable exceptions only requires modifying the retry policy configuration, not the core retry execution logic.

The org.springframework.amqp.support.converter.MessageConversionException is available on the classpath when the Rabbit transport is configured, resolving the ClassNotFoundException issue described in U2 by ensuring the correct AMQP library is included in the Rabbit transport classpath.
